disease_label_per_paper: Chikungunya fever in a kidney transplant recipient
presentation_summary: 42-year-old woman with living donor kidney transplantation seven years earlier presented with fever up to 40 C since the day before admission.
She had severe pain in both knees and the right shoulder, plus one episode of diarrhea five days earlier.
She had traveled 20 days earlier to the countryside of Paraiba in Northeast Brazil, where there was a local chikungunya outbreak.
Physical examination showed no objective arthritis, no cutaneous rash, no respiratory distress, and normal neurologic exam.

Admission labs showed creatinine 1.64 mg/dL above baseline 1.00 mg/dL, WBC 7.0 x10^9/L, absolute lymphocytes 0.28 x10^9/L, platelets 125 x10^9/L, CRP 8.08 mg/dL, ALT 81 U/L, AST 55 U/L, and CK 143 U/L.
Dengue NS1 rapid test was negative, chikungunya IgM was positive, and qualitative chikungunya RT-PCR was detectable.
Mycophenolate dose was reduced, sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim prophylaxis was stopped because of lymphopenia, and the patient received venous and oral hydration with recovery of graft function.
After two years she had creatinine 0.92 mg/dL, no chronic arthritis or bone deformation, but reported body cramps until one year after infection.

quality_warnings: Objective arthritis and rash were explicitly absent and are encoded as zero rather than omitted.
CRP was reported in mg/dL and converted to mg/L.
CHIKV IgM and RT-PCR are kept as microbiology axes because pathogen identity is not inferable from routine labs alone.
